transcript.sourceText: THE CORE IDEA
transcript.text: THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: Monopolistic competition combines many firms and relatively easy entry with differentiated products and limited price-setting power. Entry and exit operate in both models. Differentiation explains why an individual firm faces downward-sloping demand despite many sellers and easy entry. The practice is differentiating the service experience rather than relying on a legal barrier or identical product. Differentiation makes the firm’s product an imperfect substitute, so its individual demand curve slopes downward.

transcript.sourceText: WORKED EXAMPLE: IDENTIFYING PRODUCT DIFFERENTIATION
transcript.text: WORKED EXAMPLE: IDENTIFYING PRODUCT DIFFERENTIATION

runs.text: A city has many coffee shops, entry is relatively easy, and each shop offers a distinct menu and atmosphere. Because customers view the shops as close but imperfect substitutes, each shop faces downward-sloping demand and has limited price-setting power. Those facts identify monopolistic competition.

THE CORE IDEA

Differentiation explains why an individual firm faces downward-sloping demand despite many sellers and easy entry.
